/-- Finite classical control over unitary steps, oracle calls and binary
projective measurements. Computation between queries is unrestricted. -/
inductive AdaptiveProgram (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (w : ℕ) where
  | output (answer : Bool)
  | unitary (U : State ι w →ₗᵢ[ℂ] State ι w) (next : AdaptiveProgram ι w)
  | query (next : AdaptiveProgram ι w)
  | measure (S : Finset (Basis ι w)) (yes no : AdaptiveProgram ι w)

/-- The query cap is syntactic: it bounds every branch on every input, including
inputs outside a promise. -/
def AdaptiveProgram.queryCap {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] {w : ℕ} :
    AdaptiveProgram ι w → ℕ
  | .output _ => 0
  | .unitary _ next => next.queryCap
  | .query next => 1 + next.queryCap
  | .measure _ yes no => max yes.queryCap no.queryCap

def QLe {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (f : PartialBool ι) (budget : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ConstantOnPromise f ∨
  ∃ (w : ℕ) (ψ₀ : State ι w) (A : AdaptiveProgram ι w),
    ‖ψ₀‖ = 1 ∧ A.queryCap ≤ budget ∧
    ∀ x b, f x = some b → (2 / 3 : ℝ) ≤ A.outputMass x ψ₀ b

noncomputable def Q {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (f : PartialBool ι) : ℕ :=
  sInf {t : ℕ | QLe f t}

/-- `N = z₁ᵀ W D_{z₂} W ⋯ W D_{z_k} (1, …, 1)ᵀ`, expanded over paths. -/
def forrelationNumerator (k t : ℕ) (z : BitInput (ForrelationCoord k t)) : ℤ :=
  ∑ path : Fin k → Fin (mValue t),
    (∏ h : Fin k, bitSign (z (h, path h))) *
    (∏ h : Fin (k - 1),
      walshSign t (path ⟨h.val, Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le h.isLt (Nat.sub_le k 1)⟩)
        (path ⟨h.val + 1, Nat.add_lt_of_lt_sub h.isLt⟩))

/-- Equation (4) with `δ = 2^(-5k)`, written as the exact integer tests of
Lemma 2.1(iii). A large negative value of `Φ` is outside the promise. -/
def P (k t : ℕ) : PartialBool (ForrelationCoord k t) := fun z =>
  let N := forrelationNumerator k t z
  let M := forrelationDenominator k t
  if (2 : ℤ) ^ (5 * k) * N ≥ M then some true
  else if (2 : ℤ) ^ (5 * k + 1) * |N| ≤ M then some false
  else none

/-- `none` marks an input outside the promise. -/
abbrev PartialBool (ι : Type) := BitInput ι → Option Bool

structure Gate (ι : Type) (earlier : ℕ) where
  left : Option (ι ⊕ Fin earlier)
  right : Option (ι ⊕ Fin earlier)
  table : Bool → Bool → Bool

structure Circuit (ι : Type) where
  size : ℕ
  gate : (g : Fin size) → Gate ι g.val
  domainOut : Fin size
  valueOut : Fin size

def totalise {ι : Type} (f : TotalBool ι) : PartialBool ι :=
  fun x => some (f x)

/-- Lemma 2.1(iii): `d = 1` iff the function is defined, and `d = 1` implies
`b` is its value, on every input. -/
structure CircuitRealises {ι : Type} (C : Circuit ι) (f : PartialBool ι) : Prop where
  exists_transcript : ∀ x, ∃ tr, GateConsistent C x tr
  correct : ∀ x tr, GateConsistent C x tr →
    (tr C.domainOut = true ↔ promised f x) ∧
    (tr C.domainOut = true → f x = some (tr C.valueOut))

/-- The four kinds of input bit: the strings `X_i`; the strings `A_{i,h}`; the
pointer bits of each cell; the transcript bits of each cell. -/
abbrev BitLoc (ℓ r S : ℕ) (κ : Type) :=
  (Column ℓ × Column ℓ) ⊕
  (Column ℓ × Fin r × κ) ⊕
  (Σ i : Column ℓ, Address r × {j : Column ℓ // j ≠ i} × Fin ℓ) ⊕
  (Column ℓ × Address r × Fin r × Fin S)

/-- Column `i` is a winner with true address `s`: `X_i` is all ones, every
`f(A_{i,h})` is defined and equals `s h`, the cell at `s` holds correct
transcripts, and its pointers find a zero in every other column. These are the
conditions around (7) and (8). -/
def WinsAt {κ : Type} (f : PartialBool κ) (C : Circuit κ) (ℓ r : ℕ)
    (x : BitInput (BitLoc ℓ r C.size κ)) (i : Column ℓ) (s : Address r) : Prop :=
  (∀ j, readX x i j = true) ∧
  (∀ h, f (readA x i h) = some (s h)) ∧
  (∀ h, GateConsistent C (readA x i h) (readTranscript x i s h)) ∧
  (∀ j : {j : Column ℓ // j ≠ i},
    readX x j.val (pointerEquiv ℓ (readPointerBit x i s j)) = false)

/-- `F_{k,m}` for `m = 4 ^ t`: `ℓ = log₂ m = 2t` and `r = ⌈20 log₂ m⌉ = 40t`.
`C` stays a parameter because the preprint specifies a construction scheme, not
one gate numbering. Family theorems quantify over circuits realising `P`. -/
noncomputable def Fkm (k t : ℕ) (C : Circuit (ForrelationCoord k t)) :
    TotalBool (BitLoc (2 * t) (40 * t) C.size (ForrelationCoord k t)) :=
  addressedF (P k t) C (2 * t) (40 * t)

/-- Equation (10): comparison probabilities are complementary, and no candidate
beats itself. No order or transitivity is assumed. -/
structure Tournament.IsComparison {ι : Type} (a : ι → ι → ℝ) : Prop where
  complementary : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → a i j + a j i = 1
  self_zero : ∀ i, a i i = 0

/-- `L = ⌊m^(1-1/k) / (log₂ m)²⌋`, equation (5). -/
noncomputable def Lvalue (k t : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ⌊Real.rpow (mValue t : ℝ) (1 - 1 / (k : ℝ)) /
    (Real.logb 2 (mValue t : ℝ)) ^ 2⌋₊

/-- `G = ⌊mL/100⌋`, equation (17). -/
def Gvalue (m L : ℕ) : ℕ := m * L / 100

/-- The external input of Lemma 2.1(i): the Bansal–Sinha randomized lower bound
for exactly this `P`, in exactly this query model. It is used as a named
hypothesis and is never an axiom. -/
def BansalSinhaLower : Prop :=
  ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ∃ t₀ : ℕ, ∀ t : ℕ, t₀ ≤ t → Lvalue k t < R (P k t)

/-- The membership condition of equation (1). -/
def UniversalPower (α : ℝ) : Prop :=
  0 ≤ α ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ f : TotalBool (Fin n),
      (R (totalise f) : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.rpow (1 + (Q (totalise f) : ℝ)) α

  | .query _ l r => 1 + max l.depth r.depth

/-- A finite mixture of decision trees. Every tree in the mixture has positive
probability, so worst-case depth below is over the support. -/
structure RandomizedProgram (ι : Type) where
  size : ℕ
  weight : Fin size → ℝ
  tree : Fin size → QueryTree ι
  weight_pos : ∀ j, 0 < weight j
  weight_sum : ∑ j, weight j = 1

def RandomizedProgram.depth {ι : Type} (A : RandomizedProgram ι) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun j => (A.tree j).depth

noncomputable def RandomizedProgram.success {ι : Type}
    (A : RandomizedProgram ι) (x : BitInput ι) (b : Bool) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j, if (A.tree j).eval x = b then A.weight j else 0

/-- Error at most 1/3 on every promised input within `budget` queries. -/
def RLe {ι : Type} (f : PartialBool ι) (budget : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : RandomizedProgram ι,
    A.depth ≤ budget ∧ ∀ x b, f x = some b → (2 / 3 : ℝ) ≤ A.success x b

/-- Randomized query complexity. `sInf ∅ = 0` in `ℕ`, so every lower bound is
proved through `RLe` and the read-all witness that makes this set nonempty. -/
noncomputable def R {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (f : PartialBool ι) : ℕ :=
  sInf {t : ℕ | RLe f t}

abbrev Basis (ι : Type) (workspace : ℕ) := ι × Bool × Fin (workspace + 1)

abbrev State (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (workspace : ℕ) :=
  EuclideanSpace ℂ (Basis ι workspace)

/-- `O_x |i, b, z⟩ = |i, b ⊕ x_i, z⟩`. The oracle is an involution, so
permuting amplitudes by it is the same as permuting basis vectors by it. -/
noncomputable def bitOracle {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] {w : ℕ}
    (x : BitInput ι) (ψ : State ι w) : State ι w :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 fun p =>
    ψ.ofLp (p.1, (if x p.1 then !p.2.1 else p.2.1), p.2.2)

/-- For every `k ≥ 2` and `m = 4^t ≥ 2^(15k+2)`, the uniform lower bound
has numerical constant `2/18225`, a factor `256` above the coarse endpoint. -/
theorem forrelation_lower_uniform_sharp
    (k t : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (ht : 15 * k + 2 ≤ 2 * t) :
    (2 / 18225 : ℝ) *
        Real.rpow (mValue t : ℝ) (1 - 1 / (k : ℝ)) /
        ((k : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.log (4 * (k : ℝ) * (mValue t : ℝ))) <
      (R (P k t) : ℝ) := by

all independent address data. It is an upper bound, with no optimality claim. -/
theorem erasedZero_le_two {μ : BitInput κ → ℝ} (hμ : ∀ x, 0 ≤ μ x)
    (hμ1 : ∑ x, μ x = 1) {G : ℕ}
    (T : QueryTree (BitLoc ℓ r S κ)) (hT : T.depth ≤ G) :
    coupledAvg μ (fun A J I => foundZero T A J I) ≤
      2 * (G : ℝ) / ((2 ^ ℓ : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 2 :=

/-- Ledger: eq-21. The paper's per-column, per-time joint-event inequality under
the complete original dummy sampling law. -/
theorem eq_21 {f : PartialBool κ} {μ : BitInput κ → ℝ} {L : ℕ}
    (hμ : ∀ x, 0 ≤ μ x) (hμ1 : ∑ x, μ x = 1)
    (hdom : ∀ x, μ x ≠ 0 → promised f x)
    (hard : ∀ U : QueryTree κ, U.depth ≤ L → treeSuccess f μ U ≤ 2 / 3)
    (T : QueryTree (BitLoc ℓ r S κ)) (i : Column ℓ) (t : ℕ) :
    avg (prodW (prodW μ)) (fun A => avg (prodW (unif ℓ)) fun J =>
      reachedCellAt f L T J A i t) ≤ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) ^ r := by

/-- Ledger: eq-2. Stronger explicit version: the same named circuit satisfies
both inequalities with `c = 1/400`, `b = 6` and the existing `budgetConst`. -/
theorem construction_family_named (l : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ l + 1) :
    ∃ t₀ : ℕ, ∀ t : ℕ, t₀ ≤ t →
      CircuitRealises (Forrelation.forrCircuit l t) (P (l + 1) t) ∧
      (Forrelation.forrCircuit l t).size ≤
        Forrelation.forrConstant (l + 1) * mValue t * (2 * t) ^ 2 ∧
      (Q (totalise (Fkm (l + 1) t (Forrelation.forrCircuit l t))) : ℝ) ≤
        (Upper.budgetConst (l + 1) : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (mValue t : ℝ) *
          (Real.logb 2 (mValue t : ℝ)) ^ 6 ∧
      (1 / 400 : ℝ) * Real.rpow (mValue t : ℝ) (2 - 1 / ((l + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) /
          (Real.logb 2 (mValue t : ℝ)) ^ 2 ≤
        (R (totalise (Fkm (l + 1) t (Forrelation.forrCircuit l t))) : ℝ) := by

/-- Randomized query complexity. `sInf ∅ = 0` in `ℕ`, so every lower bound is

noncomputable def R {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (f : PartialBool ι) : ℕ :=
  sInf {t : ℕ | RLe f t}

/-- `O_x |i, b, z⟩ = |i, b ⊕ x_i, z⟩`. The oracle is an involution, so
permuting amplitudes by it is the same as permuting basis vectors by it. -/
noncomputable def bitOracle {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] {w : ℕ}
    (x : BitInput ι) (ψ : State ι w) : State ι w :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 fun p =>
    ψ.ofLp (p.1, (if x p.1 then !p.2.1 else p.2.1), p.2.2)
